data.name: Geetanjali
data.gender_notes: Geetanjali is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Geetanjali is derived from two Sanskrit words – Geeta (song) and Jali (flowers). The name symbolizes the flow of spiritual songs or mantras, which is a source of enlightenment and knowledge. In Hindu mythology, this name is associated with Saraswati, the goddess of wisdom and knowledge. The name Geetanjali carries the meaning “Song of the God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Geetanjali usually hope their child will grow to embody song of the god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Flowers of spiritual wisdom and knowledge
data.etymology: Geetanjali belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Song of the God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Geetanjali total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.reference: Geetanjali was the pen name of Rabindranath Tagore's wife, Joshoodhani Debi. She is best known for her poetry, especially her Bengali translations of the Srimad Bhagavad Gita and Mahabharata.
historical_references.context: Geetanjali was a major contributor to the Bengali literary scene, and her translations helped bring the ancient Indian epic texts to a wider audience.

historical_references.reference: Geetanjali was also the name of a renowned Indian actress and director, Geetanjali Gadh. She was born in 1945 in Mumbai, India, and began her career in theatre in the 1960s. She later went on to direct films and became a prominent figure in the Indian film industry.
historical_references.context: Geetanjali Gadh's contributions to Indian cinema helped to break down gender stereotypes and pave the way for more women to enter the industry as directors and actors.
